source_documents.title: Aggregation-Induced Emission: Effects of Molecular Structure, Solid-State Conformation, and Morphological Packing Arrangement on Light-Emitting Behaviors of Diphenyldibenzofulvene Derivatives
A conical intersection model to explain aggregation induced emission in diphenyl dibenzofulvene

reference_evidence_units.quote: Propeller-shaped molecules diphenyldibenzofulvene (1) and (4-methoxyphenyl)phenyldibenzofulvene (2) were nonemissive when dissolved in good solvents but became luminescent when aggregated in poor solvents or in the solid state

8-Phenylbenzo[e]acephenanthrylene (3), a ring-closed form of 1 with one of its phenyl blades locked, was emissive in the solutions, suggesting that the AIE effects of 1 and 2 are caused by the restrictions of intramolecular rotations of their aromatic blades in the aggregation state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1 vs locked 3
reference_evidence_units.statement: Locking one blade makes the dye emissive in solution.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In the solid state, intramolecular rotations of the molecules of 1 and 2 are physically restricted, which opens their radiative decay channels, hence their observed AIE effects.
In solution, the seam is accessed through rotation around the exocyclic fulvene bond, leading to radiationless decay to the ground state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1 (DPDBF)
reference_evidence_units.statement: Rotation about the exocyclic bond reaches a conical intersection seam.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Restricted rotation of the phenyl blades (exocyclic bond) blocks access to the conical intersection; the locked analogue emits in solution.
